Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Ceres discovered?
Ceres is a dwarf planet in the main asteroid belt between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
Azithromycin: Pfizer. It is administered by mouth, into a vein, or as topical treatment for the eye.
In which country is Royal Society?
Royal Society: United Kingdom. Founded on 28 November 1660, it was granted a royal charter by King Charles II and is the oldest continuously existing scientific academy in the world.
Who is credited with discovering Archaeopteryx?
Archaeopteryx: Carl Friedrich Häberlein. Archaeopteryx (lit. 'ancient wing'), sometimes referred to by its German name, "Urvogel " (lit. 'Primeval Bird') is an extinct genus of bird-like dinosaurs.
Who is credited with discovering Oganesson?
Oganesson: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Who is credited with discovering Cimetidine?
Cimetidine: John Colin Emmett. Cimetidine, sold under the brand name Tagamet among others, is a histamine H2 receptor antagonist that inhibits stomach acid production.
Who is credited with discovering Iridium?
Iridium: Smithson Tennant. Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
An economist who once worked for the IMF and later served as Prime Minister of Côte d'Ivoire from 1990 to 1993, this politician has been the country's president since 2010 — name this leader?
Alassane Ouattara (French; born 1 January 1942) is an Ivorian politician and economist who has been President of Ivory Coast (Cte d'Ivoire) since 2010.
This English number theorist became a mathematical legend by proving Fermat's Last Theorem, earning the 2016 Abel Prize and a knighthood. Who is he?
Andrew Wiles (born 11 April 1953) is an English mathematician and a Royal Society Research Professor at the University of Oxford, specialising in number theory.
This mid-sized zodiac constellation, sitting between Pisces and Taurus, has represented a ram since late Babylonian times — though its stars once formed a farmhand. Which one is it?
Aries (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. It is located in the Northern celestial hemisphere between Pisces to the west and Taurus to the east.
This large bird of prey is the only known vertebrate whose diet consists mostly — 70 to 90 percent — of bone. What bird is it?
Bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus), also known as the lammergeier and ossifrage, is a very large bird of prey in the monotypic genus Gypaetus.
Around 2,500 species of this insect family defend themselves by secreting a skin-irritating toxin called cantharidin, often flaunting bold warning colors — which family?
Blister beetle are beetles of the family Meloidae, so called for their defensive secretion of a blistering agent, cantharidin.

This British dog breed of mastiff type has a stocky build, a large head, thick facial skin folds, and a protruding lower jaw, and is now illegal to breed in the Netherlands over health concerns — name the breed?
Bulldog is a British breed of dog of mastiff type. It may also be known as the English Bulldog or British Bulldog.
This Mexican business magnate was ranked the richest person in the world by Forbes from 2010 to 2013, building his fortune through a sprawling conglomerate called Grupo Carso. Who is he?
Carlos Slim (born 28 January 1940) is a Mexican business oligarch, investor and philanthropist.

Sold under the brand name Thorazine, this phenothiazine antipsychotic treats schizophrenia and bipolar disorder — but it's also been used for nausea, pre-surgery anxiety, and even stubborn hiccups. What is it?
Chlorpromazine (CPZ), marketed under the brand names Thorazine and Largactil among others, is an antipsychotic medication.

This highly venomous, nocturnal snake, black or bluish-black with narrow white crossbands, is widely distributed across South Asia, from grasslands to agricultural fields to human settlements — what snake is it?
Common krait (Bungarus caeruleus) is a highly venomous snake species belonging to the genus Bungarus in the family Elapidae.
The third most-produced American fighter of the Second World War, trailing only the Mustang and the Thunderbolt, this plane first took flight in 1938 — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
First discovered in 1877 and named the following year for its unique double-beamed tail bones, this genus of long-necked sauropod dinosaur roamed Late Jurassic North America — what is it?
Diplodocus (or) is an extinct genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaurs known from the Late Jurassic of North America.
These extinct flightless giants of Madagascar — possibly the largest birds ever, laying the biggest eggs of any amniote — vanished around 1000 AD, likely thanks to humans. What are they called?
Elephant bird are extinct flightless birds belonging to the order Aepyornithiformes that were native to the island of Madagascar.
Known regionally in Shropshire as the 'plum bird,' this small European finch, scientifically Pyrrhula pyrrhula, was the original bird to carry its common English name — which species?
Eurasian bullfinch (Pyrrhula pyrrhula) is a small passerine bird in the finch family, Fringillidae.
Part of the dog family yet famous for a pointed snout and a brush-like tail, the 'true' members of this group belong to the genus Vulpes — what creature is it?
Fox are small-to-medium-sized omnivorous mammals belonging to several genera of the family Canidae.

Sometimes called the 'lesser apes' to distinguish them from chimpanzees, gorillas, and orangutans, these smaller, tailless primates live in forests from eastern Bangladesh through Southeast Asia and don't build nests — what are they?
Gibbon are apes in the family Hylobatidae (hylobatids).
What protein filament, grown from follicles in the skin's dermis layer and composed mainly of alpha-keratin, is one of the defining characteristics of mammals?
Hair is a protein filament that grows from follicles found in the dermis.

Known taxonomically as Lonicera, this genus of 158 species of arching shrubs and twining vines is native to northern latitudes worldwide, though one of its Asian members has become a notorious invasive pest — what's the plant?
Honeysuckle are arching shrubs or twining vines in the genus Lonicera of the family Caprifoliaceae.
Supplied by the lumbar spinal nerves and part of the femoral nerve, this fused pair of abdominal and thigh muscles is the body's strongest hip flexor — what is it called?
Iliopsoas (from Latin ile 'groin' and Ancient Greek (ps) 'muscles of the loins') refers to the joined psoas major and the iliacus muscles.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
Diagnosed via corneal topography and linked to frequent eye rubbing and allergies, this progressive disorder causes the cornea to bulge into a cone shape — which eye condition?
Keratoconus is an eye disorder in which the cornea, the transparent front part of the eye, gradually thins and bulges outward into a cone shape.
Distinguished from its cousins the pikas by short furry tails and elongated ears and hind legs, this mammal family comprises over 70 species we commonly call rabbits and hares — which family?
Leporidae is the family of rabbits and hares (Lepus), containing over 70 species of extant mammals in all.
Serving under Chancellor Adenauer, this economist championed West Germany's postwar economic miracle before becoming chancellor himself in 1963 — who is he?
Ludwig Erhard (4 February 1897 - 5 May 1977) was a German politician and economist who served as the second chancellor of West Germany from 1963 until 1966.
The heaviest and largest members of the squirrel family, these 15 species of grazing ground-dwellers vanish each winter to hibernate underground — what are they?
Marmot are large ground squirrels in the genus Marmota, with 15 species living in Asia, Europe, and North America.

Credited with discovering both the atmosphere of Venus and the law of conservation of mass in chemical reactions, this Russian polymath was also a poet who helped shape the modern Russian literary language and is considered a founder of modern geology — who is he?
Diagnosed after a speech assessment, this condition can stem from psychological trauma or a neurological disorder and isn't always permanent — what is it called?
Muteness is defined as an absence of speech, with or without an ability to hear the speech of others.

Considered primary if a child has never had a long dry stretch, this common childhood condition — usually a developmental delay rather than an illness — is commonly called bedwetting. What's its clinical name?
Nocturnal enuresis (NE), also informally called bedwetting, is involuntary urination while asleep after the age at which bladder control usually begins.
Dubbed the father of nuclear chemistry, he studied under Ernest Rutherford before helping identify the radioactive elements radium, thorium, and protactinium — who is he?
Otto Hahn (8 March 1879 - 28 July 1968) was a German chemist who was a pioneer in the field of radiochemistry.
Listed in the Dictionary of Fungi as containing over 300 species, this mold genus produces a compound that stops bacterial growth and also flavors certain cheeses — which genus?
Penicillium is a genus of ascomycetous fungi that is part of the mycobiome of many species and is of major importance in the natural environment, in food spoilage, and in food and drug production.
Equal to one-eighth of a gallon in both the imperial and US customary systems, this unit of volume is just over 20% larger in Britain than it is in America — name it?
Pint (symbol pt, sometimes abbreviated as p) is a unit of volume or capacity in both the imperial and United States customary measurement systems.

This male sexual dysfunction occurs when orgasm happens very soon after minimal sexual stimulation, with medical experts generally setting the threshold at around one minute — what's this condition called?

Premature ejaculation (PE) is a male sexual dysfunction that occurs when a male expels semen (and most likely experiences orgasm) soon after beginning sexual activity, and with minimal penile stimulation.
This colorless, odorless radioactive noble gas has the atomic number 86, and its longest-lived isotope has a half-life of under four days — name the element?
Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Known by the common name 'dog rose,' this climbing wild rose species is native across Europe and stretches into northwest Africa and western Asia — which species?
Rosa canina is a variable climbing, wild rose species native to Europe, northwest Africa, and western Asia.

These pinnipeds, distinguished from true seals by their external ear flaps and ability to walk on all fours, belong to the eared-seal family alongside fur seals, with six living species worldwide. What animal is this?
Sea lion are pinnipeds characterized by external ear flaps, long foreflippers, the ability to walk on all fours, short and thick hair, and a big chest and belly.
Which urban model uses digital technology and data from citizens, buildings, and cameras to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion?
Smart city is an urban model that leverages technology, human capital, and governance to improve sustainability, efficiency, and social inclusion, which are considered goals for cities of the future.
Known by his online username 'spez,' this web developer co-founded an airfare search engine before leading the world's seventh most-visited website as CEO — who is he?
Steve Huffman (born 1983 or 1984), also known by his Reddit username spez, is an American web developer and entrepreneur.
Symbol Tc, atomic number 43: this silvery-gray metal is entirely synthetic, though tiny natural traces form via neutron capture in molybdenum ore — what element?
Technetium is a chemical element; it has symbol Tc and atomic number 43.
A nightshade-family relative of tobacco and the potato, this South American native arrived in Eurasia via the Columbian exchange and is botanically a berry eaten as a vegetable — what is it?
Tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) is a plant whose fruit is an edible berry that is eaten as a vegetable.
This medical condition involves involuntary muscle spasms that interfere with vaginal intercourse or other penetration, often causing pain from the first attempt — what is it?
Vaginismus is a condition in which involuntary muscle spasm interferes with vaginal intercourse or other penetration of the vagina.

Dubbed the "father of English geology," this man created the first detailed geological map of an entire country — yet his humble background got him snubbed by scientists and even landed him in debtors' prison. Who was he?
William Smith (geologist) (23 March 1769 - 28 August 1839) was an English geologist, credited with creating the first detailed, nationwide geological map of any country.
This American psychologist devised a pyramid-shaped theory of human needs culminating in self-actualization, and was later ranked the 10th most-cited psychologist of the 20th century — who is he?

First flown as a stretched derivative of a popular narrow-body jet family in 1994, this twin-engine airliner carries up to 239 passengers and later gained a fuel-efficient 'neo' version with new winglets — which aircraft?
Airbus A321: Airliner, stretched model of the A320 family.

The brightest star in the constellation Aquila and a vertex of the Summer Triangle, this nearby A-type star spins so fast — about 286 km/s at its equator — that it bulges noticeably. Which star is it?
Altair: Brightest star in the constellation Aquila. Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky.

Affecting about 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder causes severe intellectual disability, little to no speech, and balance problems — yet those affected are often noted for a notably happy personality. Which condition is it?
Angelman syndrome: Genetic disorder caused by a mutation of chromosome 15.
Also known as pirarucu or paiche, this native of the Amazon River basin is among the largest freshwater fish on Earth — what species is it?
The third-largest fish in its family, behind Siberian taimen and Pacific Chinook, this species is unusual for surviving spawning and returning to sea to breed again — which fish?
Atlantic salmon: Species of fish. The Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar) is a species of ray-finned fish in the family Salmonidae.
Second only to the capybara among living rodents and able to top 50 kg, this animal sports chisel-like incisors, webbed back feet, and a flat, scaly tail — what is it?

A natural cross between the pomelo and the wild mandarin, this Southeast Asian citrus is too sour to eat off the tree — but the Seville variety is exactly what British cooks prize for their breakfast preserve. What fruit is it?

When a gas of bosons is cooled to within a hair of absolute zero, this state of matter, first predicted in 1924-25, sees a large fraction of particles pile into a single quantum state — what is it called?
Bose–Einstein condensate: State of matter. In 1995, the Bose–Einstein condensate was created by Eric Cornell and Carl Wieman of the University of Colorado Boulder using rubidium atoms.
Belonging to the superfamily Papilionoidea, these brightly winged insects pass through a chrysalis stage, and their oldest fossils date to about 56 million years ago — what are they?
Butterfly: Group of insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.
Packed with chlorophyll, this plant-cell organelle captures sunlight, splits water to release oxygen, and feeds sugar-making in the Calvin cycle — what is it called?
Chloroplast: Plant organelle that conducts photosynthesis.
A tropane alkaloid drawn from the leaves of South American coca plants, it once served doctors as a local anesthetic with handy vasoconstricting properties — what is this stimulant?

Cocaine: Tropane alkaloid and stimulant drug. The leaves are processed into cocaine paste, a crude mixture of coca alkaloids, from which cocaine base is isolated and then converted to cocaine hydrochloride.
The first bomber capable of Mach 2 flight, this 1950s delta-winged bomber carried its nuclear payload in a combination bomb-and-fuel pod slung beneath the fuselage — which bomber?
Convair B-58 Hustler: Cold War-era American supersonic bomber.

First described by Linnaeus in 1767, this citrus-family plant native to the Indian subcontinent has aromatic leaves essential to South Asian cooking, especially in India and Sri Lanka — which species?

Curry tree: Species of flowering plant. It is native to the Indian subcontinent, southern China and mainland Southeast Asia, and it has been introduced to other parts of southeast Asia and to Australia.
Nicknamed the 'gympie-gympie' by Queensland's Gubbi Gubbi people, this Australian and Malaysian rainforest plant delivers an infamously painful, long-lasting sting. What species is it?
Dendrocnide moroides: Species of plant in the nettle family.
A Canadian optical physicist at Waterloo, she shared the 2018 Nobel in Physics for the practical implementation of chirped pulse amplification — who is she?
Donna Strickland: Canadian physicist, engineer, and Nobel laureate.
Belonging to the order Anguilliformes and comprising roughly 1,000 species, these ray-finned predators transform dramatically from larva to adult and mostly live in salt water — what are they?
This fungal genus growing on rye and other cereals produces alkaloids that cause a poisoning condition in humans and livestock who eat contaminated grain — which group of fungi?
Ergot: Fungi of the genus Claviceps. The most prominent member of this group is Claviceps purpurea (rye ergot fungus).

Its mating has never once been observed in the wild, and its five life stages were once mistaken for five separate species — this critically endangered fish is threatened by dams and overfishing. What is it?
European eel: Species of fish. The five stages of their development were originally thought to be different species.
Known as the weeping fig and the official tree of Bangkok, this flowering plant native to Asia and Australia is often used as a biomonitor in cities — which species?
Ficus benjamina: Species of fig. The species is also naturalized in the West Indies and in the states of Florida and Arizona in the United States.
Working in Feynman's group on the Manhattan Project before co-detecting an elusive elementary particle with Clyde Cowan, he won the 1995 Nobel for catching the neutrino — who was he?
Combining Greek words for 'earth,' 'form,' and 'study,' what field examines how landscapes and seafloor features form and evolve over time?
With DNA up to 99% identical to ours, this troop-dwelling great ape — led by a dominant 'silverback' — is the largest living primate on Earth — what is it?
Gorilla: Genus of large African apes.
First described in 1893 during a flu pandemic and mistakenly blamed as its cause, this Gram-negative bacterium causes pneumonia and meningitis mainly in infants — which bacterium?
Haemophilus influenzae: Species of bacterium. The bacteria are mesophilic and grow best at temperatures between 35 and 37 °C.
Introduced to Britain in the 19th century as an ornamental plant, this Caucasus-native's sap causes painful blistering burns when exposed skin meets sunlight — which species?
Heracleum mantegazzianum: Species of flowering plant. Heracleum mantegazzianum, commonly known as giant hogweed, is a monocarpic perennial herbaceous plant in the carrot family Apiaceae.

In the Renaissance this field of study covered classical literature and language rather than religion or divinity, and today it groups subjects using critical and interpretive methods rather than empirical ones — what broad academic category is this?
Humanities: Academic disciplines that study society and culture.

Trained originally as a naval architect before becoming a self-taught nuclear physicist, this scientist directed the Soviet Union's atomic bomb program and earned the nickname 'father of the Russian bomb' — who is he?
This tech entrepreneur co-founded Twitter, later built a fintech company behind Square, Cash App, and Tidal, and also helped launch the decentralized network Bluesky?
This English scientist's 1808 book, 'A New System of Chemical Philosophy,' laid the foundations of modern atomic theory, and he also kept daily weather records for over fifty years — who was he?
John Dalton: British chemist and physicist (1766–1844)
Patented in 1967 and approved for medical use in 1980, this propionic-acid-class NSAID works by blocking prostaglandin production — what is it?
Described both as a science and as the art of justice, this set of enforced rules can be made by legislatures, executive decrees or judges' precedent — what is it?
A sweet, aromatic flavouring used in confectionery, tobacco, and pharmaceuticals comes from the root of which legume — though more than a couple of milligrams per kilo a day can cause trouble?
Often a complication of cancer treatment, this incurable, progressive swelling condition is managed with compression therapy and manual drainage rather than diuretics — what is it?
Lymphedema: Swelling due to a compromised lymphatic system.

The first woman to write a mathematics handbook and the first appointed as a university math professor, this Milanese scholar later traded calculus for four decades of theology and charity — who is she?
Maria Gaetana Agnesi: Italian mathematician and philanthropist (1718–1799)
Triggered by falling progesterone, this regular discharge from the uterine lining signals that pregnancy hasn't occurred, and typically first arrives at menarche between ages 11 and 13 — what is it?
Menstruation: Periodic shedding of the uterine lining.
Based on a Soviet fighter jet but optimized for ground attack, this variable-sweep aircraft was license-built in India as the 'Bahadur,' or 'Valiant' — which jet?
Mikoyan MiG-27: Series of 1970s Soviet attack aircraft.

First identified from skulls found in a Dutch chalk quarry near Maastricht and initially mistaken for crocodile or whale bones, this giant marine lizard genus lived until 66 million years ago — which genus is it?
Mosasaurus: Extinct genus of marine lizard from the Late Cretaceous.
Colloquially known as a moon, this type of astronomical body orbits a planet or dwarf planet, with 455 confirmed examples across the Solar System's six major systems — what is it called?
Natural satellite: Astronomical body that orbits a planet. Natural satellites are colloquially referred to as moons, by analogy with the Moon, Earth's natural satellite.
Born in New York to Holocaust-survivor parents, this political scientist made the politics of the Holocaust and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict his life's work. Who is he?
This medical specialty trains physicians for four years after medical school to diagnose, medically treat, and surgically correct eye disease — what is it?
Ophthalmology: Field of medicine treating eye disorders.
Credited as the 'father of toxicology,' this Swiss Renaissance physician and alchemist also wrote prophetic 'Prognostications' later studied by Rosicrucians — who is he?
Paracelsus: Swiss physician, philosopher, theologian, and alchemist (c. 1493 – 1541)
This inflammation of the sac surrounding the heart causes sharp chest pain that eases when sitting up and worsens when lying down or breathing deeply — what condition is it?
Pericarditis: Inflammation of the pericardium. Pericarditis (PER-i-kar-DYE-tis) is inflammation of the pericardium, the fibrous sac surrounding the heart.
Boasting the longest cones of any spruce and widely planted as a Christmas tree, this European conifer was also the first gymnosperm to have its genome sequenced — which species?
Picea abies: Species of plant. Picea abies, the Norway spruce, Norway fir or European spruce, is a species of spruce native to Northern, Central and Eastern Europe.
Born Joseph Ratzinger, this head of the Catholic Church made history in 2013 by resigning the role, then adopted the title 'emeritus' until his death — who was he?
Pope Benedict XVI: Head of the Catholic Church from 2005 to 2013.
Flagged by the WHO as one of the greatest antibiotic-resistance threats to humans, this rod-shaped bacterium causes hospital infections like ventilator-associated pneumonia — which pathogen?
Pseudomonas aeruginosa: Species of bacterium. P. aeruginosa is able to selectively inhibit various antibiotics from penetrating its outer membrane and has high resistance to several antibiotics.
Named for the ragged look of its leaves, this genus of flowering plants causes up to half of all pollen-related allergy cases despite a genus name meaning 'food of the gods' — which plant?
Ragweed: Genus of plants. The name "ragweed" is derived from "ragged" + "weed," coming from the ragged appearance of the plant's leaves.
Also called vitamin B2, this nutrient forms two key coenzymes for energy metabolism, can be prescribed for corneal thinning, and taken orally may cut down migraines in adults — which vitamin is it?
Riboflavin: Vitamin, dietary supplement, and yellow food dye.

Nicknamed 'The Kite' (or perhaps 'The Dragon'), this Swedish supersonic fighter-interceptor's innovative double-delta wing traces back to 1948 and entered frontline service in March 1960 — which aircraft?
Saab 35 Draken: 1955 Swedish fighter aircraft. The full-scale production version entered service with frontline squadrons of the Swedish Air Force on 8 March 1960.
Native to cold-temperate Eurasia, this spiny deciduous shrub yields a fruit and oil prized in both cooking and cosmetics — what plant is it?
Sea buckthorn: Species of flowering plant in the family Elaeagnaceae.
Sitting just below carbon in group 14 of the periodic table, this blue-grey, brittle semiconductor is essential to plants and dominates the world's transistors and solar cells — which element is it?
Silicon: Chemical element with atomic number 14 (Si)
Known by nicknames like 'garden' and 'lamb,' and native from Ireland to southern China, which herb's aromatic oil flavors food, teas, and various scents?
Spearmint: Plant species in the mint family.

Named from Greek words meaning 'a chain of berries' and 'pus-forming,' this Gram-positive bacterial species is the predominant carrier of the Lancefield group A antigen, often abbreviated GAS — what is this bacterium's full scientific name?
Streptococcus pyogenes: Species of bacterium. The name group A (beta-hemolytic) Streptococcus is thus also used.
These astringent polyphenolic compounds bind proteins and are found abundantly in oak bark, historically used to turn animal hides into leather — what are they?
Tannin: Class of astringent, bitter plant polyphenolic chemical compounds.

Grain processing strips so much of this micronutrient that many countries enrich their flours to replace it; a deficiency leads to beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy. Also known as vitamin B1, which essential nutrient is it?
Thiamine: Chemical compound and essential nutrient.
Linked to the use of highly absorbent tampons, this bacterial-toxin condition causes fever, rash, skin peeling, and a dangerous drop in blood pressure — which condition?
Toxic shock syndrome: Medical condition caused by bacterial toxins.
One of the two main inflammatory bowel diseases, this long-term condition inflames and ulcerates the colon and rectum, causing abdominal pain and bloody diarrhea — what is it?
Ulcerative colitis: Inflammatory bowel disease that causes ulcers in the colon.
This ability to detect light and turn it into an image of one's surroundings can occur via daytime or night vision — what is it called?
Visual perception: Ability to interpret the surrounding environment using light in the visible spectrum.

Caused by the deletion of about 27 genes on chromosome 7, this genetic disorder is known for an unusually outgoing, empathetic personality alongside visual-spatial learning challenges — which condition?
Williams syndrome: Genetic disorder. Williams syndrome (WS), also Williams–Beuren syndrome (WBS), is a genetic disorder that affects many parts of the body.
Fluorine is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for fluorine is F. Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
What is the chemical symbol for cerium?
The symbol for cerium is Ce. Cerium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ce and atomic number 58, and is a soft, ductile, and silvery-white metal that tarnishes when exposed to air.
